clue.text: Warner set enclosing concrete area

indicators.note: enclosing means the word for set wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: set, as in firm or rigid

explanation.surface: Someone sets concrete around a builder's yard, under a mysterious name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warner' looks like a surname; it is simply something that warns.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that sounds to alert people to a blaze is literally a thing that gives warning.

clue.text: Round insect doesn't come up to scratch birds

indicators.note: round placed before the insect says the other word goes round it

parts.note: to fail is not to come up to scratch

explanation.surface: A circling bug is found wanting, and so are some birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy pigeons and flycatchers with spread, fan-shaped tails go by this name.

clue.text: Bookmaker, say, turning up amid nonsense, rubbish, drivel, claptrap etc

indicators.note: amid means the reversed piece sits in the middle of the word for nonsense

parts.note: rot is a word for all of these

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A list of synonyms for twaddle, like a thesaurus entry, with a bookie somewhere in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests a bookie; it is a compiler of a book, and the list of synonyms is itself a thesaurus joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous thesaurus, so he literally made a book.

clue.text: Flora's active in going to pot plants

indicators.note: going to pot means falling into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the name read with its S

explanation.surface: Flora is busy potting up some plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' looks like a woman's name or plant life; it is anagram fodder, and 'going to pot' doubles as potting plants.
explanation.definitionFit: These small houseplants with velvety leaves are a popular kind of flowering pot plant.

clue.text: Redcoat going bust in style …

indicators.note: going bust means breaking apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British soldier's career collapses in a stylish way.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a decorative design movement of the 1920s and 1930s, a style of art and architecture.

clue.text: … manages to forge small note

parts.note: do (doh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone gets by by forging a little banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning copes or gets by with limited resources.

clue.text: Exploited figures in Rousseau's education

indicators.note: figures in means the letters appear inside the following words

explanation.surface: Something exploited features in the philosopher's educational writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something taken advantage of has been made use of.

clue.text: Fare from the junction?

parts.note: a dish of long pasta named after Birmingham's famously tangled motorway interchange

explanation.surface: Food served at a railway junction.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravelly Hill Interchange in Birmingham, England, is nicknamed after a pasta because of its tangled loops.
explanation.definitionFit: This pasta is fare, and it lends its name to a famously tangled road junction.

clue.text: Minder fitting girl up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the name is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A minder fitting a girl up, as in framing her.
explanation.definitionFit: An older woman acting as chaperone to a young girl, especially in Spain, is a minder.

clue.text: Criminal from a timely spy movie

indicators.note: criminal suggests wrongdoing, so the letters are put to bad, scrambled use

explanation.surface: A crook comes out of a topical spy film.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1971 Clint Eastwood thriller is a film.

clue.text: Country backing queen mostly

indicators.note: backing means the trimmed word is read in reverse
mostly means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A nation supports its queen, on the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letter of REGINA to get REGIN, then reverse it.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked West African state, named after the river.

clue.text: Say farewell, having heard Scottish runner split

indicators.note: having heard says the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river (runner), and to cleave is to split

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye after hearing a Scottish athlete had broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete but is a river; the Tay is Scotland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for departing politely, bidding goodbye.

clue.text: Possibly an item

definitions.meaning: 'an' is an example of a grammatical word of this kind, the indefinite one
an item, as in an object or a piece in a newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: Grammarians call 'a', 'an' and 'the' by this name, and it also means a thing or a piece of writing.

clue.text: Tell me to stop being windy as he yawns

indicators.note: windy suggests things being blown about, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be stopped from going on, as the listener yawns.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase used when pouring a drink: tell me when you want me to stop.

clue.text: Got silly organ? Fancy seeing a specialist?

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, but as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone whose organ has gone silly considers seeing a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A throat doctor is a medical specialist dealing with the voice box.

clue.text: New layout incorporating new flag

indicators.note: incorporating means the word for new layout takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a new layout is a redesign

explanation.surface: A new layout includes a new flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The red ensign is the flag flown by British merchant ships.

clue.text: Empty sack engraver found in drawer

indicators.note: empty means the middle of the word is removed, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: An empty sack and an engraver turn up in a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like furniture; it is a person who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: One who draws pictures, an artist making rough drawings.

clue.text: Working — like David Copperfield?

definitions.meaning: David Copperfield is an American stage magician, performing an illusion

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being effective, which read literally describes a magician performing.

clue.text: Lose bearings on your bike!

definitions.meaning: British slang telling someone to go away

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to stray from your way and, as a rude command, clear off.

clue.text: For a magpie it's more distressing when nothing is retained

indicators.note: is retained means the zero is kept inside the comparative word

explanation.surface: Losing nothing would be harder for a bird that collects things.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a magpie is a person who collects and keeps things compulsively.

clue.text: Believe it's on the cards?

explanation.definitionFit: To trust something as true, and also the borrowing a credit card gives.

clue.text: Butterfly allowed to follow band

indicators.note: to follow means the word for allowed comes after the word for band

explanation.surface: A butterfly is permitted to trail after a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringlet is a brown British butterfly with small eye-spots.

clue.text: Trees planted in the middle of Seattle in the early stages

indicators.note: planted in means the trees are set inside the other letters
the middle of means the central letters of the city name

explanation.surface: Trees were planted in central Seattle early on.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning initially, at the beginning.

clue.text: Food cooked in oven or pan

definitions.meaning: a joint of meat cooked for a meal
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.definitionFit: A word for a joint of meat, for baking it in an oven, and for slating someone.

clue.text: Doctor, having provided couple with excess of drugs, may be washed up

explanation.surface: A doctor who gave a pair an overdose may be finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washed up' suggests a ruined career; it is literally deposited on shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood floating on the sea is what tends to be deposited on beaches.

clue.text: Get to church on time, switching leaders

indicators.note: switching leaders means the first two letters change places
on means the church abbreviation is placed after the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Arrive at church punctually, with leaders swapped round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching leaders' means the first two letters of ERACH change places, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to reach a place is to arrive at it.

clue.text: Loaf brought round with a fish

indicators.note: brought round means the word for head is turned back to front

parts.note: loaf is slang for head, as is nut

explanation.surface: A loaf of bread is brought with a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' looks like bread; in slang (from loaf of bread, head) it means head.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ocean fish, often canned.

clue.text: One harasses people in Twin Peaks

indicators.note: in means people are placed inside the doubled hill word
twin means the hill word appears twice

parts.note: a tor is a rocky peak

explanation.surface: Someone harasses the townsfolk in the TV series Twin Peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Twin Peaks is a TV series; here it means two tors.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who torments is one who harasses or persecutes.
